title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale, eggs, and Pecorino
excerpt: Spaghetti tossed with crisp guanciale, beaten egg yolks, and Pecorino Romano to create a silky, rich sauce without any cream. The technique is everything: the eggs must not scramble.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carbonara is a Roman pasta dish whose origins are debated but most likely date to the mid-20th century. The canonical ingredients are guanciale (cured pork cheek), Pecorino Romano, eggs, black pepper, and pasta. Pancetta is a widely used substitute for guanciale outside Italy; the two are interchangeable in this recipe though guanciale has a richer flavour. The dish contains no cream: the sauce is made entirely from the emulsification of eggs, fat, cheese, and pasta water. The key challenge is creating a smooth sauce without scrambling the eggs, which requires removing the pan from the heat before adding the egg mixture.

recipeTools.notes: For the pasta and for mixing the carbonara.

content.text: The technique is precise: cook the guanciale until crisp, remove the pan from the heat, add the drained pasta, then add the egg and cheese mixture off the heat, tossing constantly and adding pasta water a little at a time to create a creamy sauce. If the pan is too hot, the eggs will scramble. Work quickly. The pasta must be fresh from the water: cold pasta will not give enough heat to form the sauce. Use a mixture of egg yolks and one whole egg for the richest result.

items.preparation: finely grated, plus extra to serve

content.text: Beat the egg yolks and whole egg with the grated Pecorino and Parmesan. Add the coarsely ground black pepper. Mix well and set aside.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve at least 200 ml of pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, fry the guanciale in a cold pan over medium heat, allowing the fat to render slowly, for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp. Remove the pan from the heat.

Add the drained spaghetti to the pan with the guanciale and fat. Toss to coat. Add a splash of pasta water and toss. Wait 30 seconds for the pan to cool slightly. Pour in the egg mixture and toss vigorously, adding pasta water a tablespoon at a time, until the sauce is creamy and coats the pasta. Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and black pepper.
